transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-15
Time: 07:00 PST / 15:00 UTC
Duration: 44 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Rajat Menon (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (TulipCore CTO), Devon Hale (Cloud Architect), Priya Nair (Partnerships), Omar Bennett (SRE)
Recordings/Links: deck link: https://redwood.app/partners/tulipcore-kickoff (shared) | security pack placeholder: to follow

Summary (auto): Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and TulipCore to evaluate onramp to TulipCore's cloud offering and potential reseller/integration. Focus on GPU routing, private deployment options, latency vs cost tradeoffs, and proofs-of-concept.

Topics discussed: partner model, Dedicated vs Hosted, VPC/private plane, KMS/encryption, autoscaling and preemption, perf benchmarks and KV cache, commercial model and SLAs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Lena, I'm the AE working with TulipCore for this partnership. Um, Rajat is our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Marta Ruiz: Good morning — good afternoon — thanks for pulling this together. We have a few folks from infra and partnerships. We'll try to keep it focused.
[00:15] Devon Hale: Morning. I wanted to flag up front: our main ask is to understand latency characteristics for batch inference on mixed sequence lengths and — uh — how Redwood would route to our cloud offering.
[00:26] Rajat Menon: Great, thanks. Quick agenda: 1) high-level platform fit, 2) routing & Dedicated options, 3) security/compliance, 4) next steps and bench plans. Sound OK?
[00:32] Marta Ruiz: Yep, go ahead.
[00:34] Lena Park: Quick context: TulipCore runs a global cloud with spot/reserved GPU pools; we're exploring a reseller/onramp partnership so Redwood would route inference traffic to TulipCore when a customer selects that provider. We're also talking private VPC options later.
[00:47] Priya Nair: From partnerships side, we're mapping GTM and margins. Technical is more about compatibility and support.
[00:52] Omar Bennett: SRE here. We care about autoscaling, preemption safety, and how the KV cache behaves when instances are recycled.

[01:05] Rajat Menon: On the runtime: Redwood supports continuous batching, prefix/KV caching, and we do quantization-aware kernel selection. In a Dedicated/reseller scenario we can either deploy a Redwood agent in TulipCore's infra or route to a tenant-safe pool. There's a few routing models: latency-first, cost-first, or tiered (enterprise -> dedicated).
[01:26] Devon Hale: Could you expand on the agent vs tenant pool? We're concerned about network egress and data residency. If there's an agent in our VPC that keeps traffic internal that's preferable.
[01:35] Rajat Menon: Yes — agent-in-VPC: Redwood control plane still manages model versions, but inference stays within your VPC, keys managed by your KMS. Tenant pool: more like a shared pool we reserve for TulipCore customers, which is simpler but may egress.
[01:49] Marta Ruiz: KMS integration is key. We cannot have customer keys leave our side. SOC2 and audit logs are must-haves for pilots.
[01:57] Lena Park: Totally — we can offer customer-managed keys in Private, and we'll share SOC2 artifacts.

[02:10] Rajat Menon: On performance, two points: 1) kernel selection depends heavily on sequence distribution; we optimize for tokens/sec but tail latencies depend on batch mixing and KV hit rates. 2) KV cache behavior: for long-running chat sessions we keep KV on warm instances; for spot preemption we persist to a local fast-backed store — we can align on TTL.
[02:34] Omar Bennett: For us, typical session length distribution: 60% short (<128 tokens), 30% medium (128-1024), 10% long (>1024). Any optimization ideas?
[02:44] Rajat Menon: That distribution is helpful. We recommend quant profiles for mixed sequences and a small warm pool for chat workloads. Also prefix caching will cut repeated token cost. We'll share a tuning doc.

[03:05] Devon Hale: How do you handle fallbacks? If TulipCore capacity is exhausted or spot instances reclaimed, does Redwood fail over to hosted models? That has implications for latency and cost to our end customers.
[03:17] Lena Park: We support smart routing and fallbacks — you can set policies: fail to alternative TulipCore-compatible model variant, route to Redwood-hosted with cost uplift, or queue with degraded SLA. Usually customers want predictable behavior configured per route.
[03:32] Marta Ruiz: Pricing & revenue share question — do you have a standard reseller model or is this bespoke?
[03:38] Lena Park: We typically start with a pilot: reserved capacity for initial customers and a revenue share for resold Hosted usage. That said we can tailor margins for enterprise commitments. We'll send sample commercial terms.

[03:55] Priya Nair: On the technical side I want clarity on supported accelerators — we run mixture of A100-ish and some upcoming H100s across zones. Any compatibility gotchas?
[04:06] Rajat Menon: We test on a range of architectures; some quant kernels differ on H100 vs A100, so perf profiles will vary. We can provide per-GPU throughput numbers during the bench. Also note we have different compilation paths for int8 vs bfloat quant.
[04:22] Devon Hale: If we do an onramp, can we require a minimum latency SLO?
[04:27] Rajat Menon: Yes, SLA-backed Dedicated can have latency targets tied to reserved pools. For Hosted routing, it's more probabilistic but still instrumented.

[05:00] Marta Ruiz: Security review — SSO, SAML, RBAC? We need integration with our enterprise IdP for admin functions and audit logs shipped to our SIEM.
[05:10] Lena Park: Redwood supports SAML SSO for console and has RBAC with audit trails. Logs can be forwarded to your SIEM or delivered as raw audit bundles. We'll share the integration guide and a sample log schema.
[05:24] Omar Bennett: What about data retention for debug logs? We have strict retention windows per region.
[05:30] Rajat Menon: We can configure retention policy per-tenant and region. In Private deployment, logs can be kept entirely on your side.

[05:45] Devon Hale: I'd like to understand the friction points for a PoC: how long to stand up a tenant agent in our VPC and run a pilot?
[05:54] Rajat Menon: If TulipCore has infra automation (terraform modules) we can deploy an agent in ~2-3 days for a simple pilot. Full network/security reviews add time — so plan 2-4 weeks end-to-end for everything.
[06:07] Marta Ruiz: That timeline seems OK. We'll need an internal calendar of checkpoints.

[06:20] Lena Park: For the bench, we'll need sample traces, a headroom target, and a list of representative models. Devon, could you share a sample workload?
[06:27] Devon Hale: Yes — we can share traces and a small corpus, but we'll need a NDA for traces that contain PII.
[06:33] Priya Nair: Commercial note: we also want to co-brand a pilot offering and have a marketing brief.
[06:40] Lena Park: Great — we'll align on GTM after technical sign-off.

[06:52] Rajat Menon: Quick technical note: preemption handling — when an instance is reclaimed we try to drain traffic and migrate KV to a warm buffer. For really latency-sensitive flows, we recommend a small hot standby pool to avoid tail spikes. That increases cost but keeps p99 low.
[07:12] Omar Bennett: On the hot standby: what's typical additional capacity we should budget? 5-15%?
[07:18] Rajat Menon: Usually 10% is a good starting point for chat-heavy workloads.

[07:30] Devon Hale: Any requirements on network egress? Our compliance team needs to know what IP ranges to allow.
[07:36] Lena Park: We'll provide a CIDR list and region-specific endpoints. For agent-in-VPC mode, there is minimal egress.

[07:48] Marta Ruiz: Do you support bringing-your-own-models? We have custom fine-tuned models for some clients.
[07:53] Rajat Menon: Yes. We can serve customer models and manage versions. We also support model pinning and can do canary rollouts and A/B traffic splits from the console or API.

[08:10] Devon Hale: On observability — token-level cost, latency breakdowns, tracing?
[08:15] Rajat Menon: Redwood Console provides per-route token cost, per-model latency histograms, and request traces with callstack hints. For Private, traces are shipped to your tracing tool via an exporter.

[08:30] Priya Nair: Any blocker for a pilot from Redwood side?
[08:33] Lena Park: Not from product side. We'll need the sample traces, a list of target customers to include in pilot, and confirmation on the agent vs tenant pool decision.

[08:45] Marta Ruiz: Let's tentatively pick agent-in-VPC for pilot — keeps keys and logs under our control.
[08:50] Omar Bennett: Agreed.

[09:00] Rajat Menon: Good. I'll outline the bench plan: 1) baseline perf on your hardware images, 2) run mixed sequence workloads with KV cache on/off, 3) simulate preemptions, 4) gather p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec.
[09:18] Devon Hale: For bench, how long do you need to run to get meaningful tail numbers?
[09:23] Rajat Menon: I'd say at least 1 hour of steady-state with periodic longer sequences injected to produce tails.

[09:35] Lena Park: We'll schedule that. Marta/Priya — can we lock a target customer set?
[09:40] Priya Nair: We'll propose two pilot customers — one eComm and one enterprise search — that'll give mixed loads.

[09:51] Marta Ruiz: On the commercial terms please include a clause for capacity reservation and an uplift for hot standby. Also a clause for support SLAs during pilot.
[09:59] Lena Park: Got it. We'll send sample terms.

[10:10] Rajat Menon: One last technical question for Devon/Omar: do you run containerized inference images or bare-metal VM workloads? That affects how the agent is deployed.
[10:19] Devon Hale: Mostly containerized on k8s with GPU device plugin, some bare-metal for H100 instances.
[10:25] Rajat Menon: Perfect — we can provide a DaemonSet and an alternative VM image.

[10:35] Marta Ruiz: Any legal procurement hurdles we should be aware of? Our procurement team often requests SCCs and Data Processing Addendum for pilot customers.
[10:43] Lena Park: We'll surface our standard DPA and can sign an SCC; legal usually turns in a week for pilots but can take longer for larger commitments.

[10:55] Devon Hale: A small nit: we've seen tokenization mismatches before when moving between runtimes — do you have a tokenizer validation step?
[11:01] Rajat Menon: Yes — part of onboarding is verifying tokenization parity, and we have a tokenization debug tool we can run against a corpus. We'll include that in the bench runbook.

[11:12] Lena Park: OK, let's recap next steps.
[11:15] Lena Park: Action items: 1) Rajat - perf spreadsheet + bench plan; 2) Lena - security pack + SOC2 and DPA; 3) Devon - sample traces and client list; 4) TulipCore legal to review DPA. We'll aim to reconvene after bench results.

[11:34] Marta Ruiz: Sounds good. Thanks everyone. We'll look for the docs and the bench schedule.
[11:40] Priya Nair: Thanks.
[11:42] Omar Bennett: Thanks all.
[11:45] Lena Park: Thanks — we'll follow up by Monday with docs and a proposed schedule.

Closing notes: Redwood committed to agent-in-VPC pilot; bench to run for 1 hour steady-state; initial pilot customers TBD by TulipCore; security pack and SOC2 artifacts to be sent by Redwood.
